title: Account Review Playbook — QBR Ops Checklist & Facilitation Primer
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, repeatable playbook for running account QBRs that surface renewal risk early, drive micro-commitments, and leave a clear ownerable follow-up plan. Designed for mid-market and enterprise accounts; intentionally prescriptive so new CS hires and solutions engineers can run effective reviews.

How to use this doc (quick):
- Copy into a customer-specific doc and replace {{PLACEHOLDERS}}.
- Run a 15–20 minute pre-brief with the AE and SE 72–48 hours before the QBR.
- Follow the timed agenda strictly; we prefer a shorter, action-first meeting vs long slide decks.

Invite list (who to invite and why):
- Executive Sponsor (customer): rationale & strategic alignment
- Primary Day-to-Day User / Product Owner: usage, blockers, roadmap needs
- Procurement/Sourcing (if renewal within 90 days): pricing/contract questions
- Account Exec (AE): commercial alignment and next-steps
- Solutions Engineer (SE) or CSM technical lead: technical risks and delivery plan
- Internal observers (optional): AM/CS manager for escalations

Pre-meeting checklist (owner / deadline):
- 10 business days out: pull last 90-day usage, latency and error trends (owner: CS ops). Attach snapshot to doc.
- 7 days out: AE confirms attendee list + target outcomes (owner: AE).
- 5 days out: SE / CSM prepares 3 success stories + 2 known pains with severity and impact estimate (owner: SE/CSM).
- 3 days out: Send calendar invite + pre-read (1 pager) and ask stakeholders to add topics (owner: CSM).
- 2 days out: Run 20-min pre-brief with AE+SE to align script (owner: CSM).

Stakeholder map (prep note):
- Map influence vs intent: High influence / Low intent = risk (requires AE focus); High intent / Low influence = champions to enable.
- Quick template: {{NAME}} — role — what success looks like for them — ask for this QBR.

Meeting agenda (45 minutes recommended — adaptable to 30 or 60):
- 0:00–0:05 — Kickoff (CSM): thanks, goals for meeting, confirm timebox and outcomes
  Script: "Thanks everyone — today’s goal is to agree on the top 3 priorities for the next 90 days and confirm renewal posture. We’ll keep this to 45 minutes; if we need more time we’ll capture follow-ups."
- 0:05–0:12 — Health snapshot (CSM): 90-day usage, SLA/latency highlights, top incidents
  Script: "Here are the signal-level trends we’re seeing. The red/yellow/green summary: <one-line verdict>."
- 0:12–0:25 — Customer perspective (customer PO): top wins, remaining blockers (facilitator cue)
  Facilitator cue: "Can you walk us through how the platform helped your team this quarter, and what’s still preventing you from broader adoption?"
- 0:25–0:35 — Risk & opportunity deep dive (SE + AE): performance tuning, feature gaps, scale needs
  Script: "We see three opportunities to reduce cost or improve latency — quick run through and estimated impact (owner + timeframe)."
- 0:35–0:42 — Decisions & micro-commitments (All): capture owners, deadlines, and measure of success
  Script: "For each priority, who will be the owner and what does success look like in 60 days?"
- 0:42–0:45 — Close & next steps (AE + CSM): confirm follow-up cadence and renewal checkpoint
  Script: "Action owners and dates are confirmed. We’ll circulate the minutes within 2 business days and set a 30-min checkpoint in 6 weeks."

Facilitation primer (practical prompts & transitions):
- Opening: state the constraint (time) and the litmus test for success (3 prioritized actions).
- If discussion stalls: use the "parking-lot" technique and propose a 1:1 deep-dive after the call.
- If stakeholder pushes pricing early: acknowledge, then surface usage & outcomes first; put pricing on the final decision block with AE.
- Pulling consensus: repeat summary and ask "are we aligned?" — if not, propose a binary next-step (pilot/extension/change scope).

Health & Renewal Radar (quick scoring to surface risk):
- CS Health score (0–100) = mix of adoption (40%), reliability (30%), advocacy (20%), commercial alignment (10%).
- Quick buckets: 80–100 green, 60–79 yellow (monitor actions), <60 red (escalation).
- Example: Adoption: low (15/40), Reliability: medium (20/30), Advocacy: high (16/20), Commercial: low (2/10) => total 53 => yellow/red borderline — triggers AE outreach within 48 hours.

Renewal conversation template (phrasing and cadence):
- Opening line: "We want to make sure Redwood continues to drive measurable value for your team. As we look toward renewal, can we align on the outcomes you expect to see by then?"
- If renewal within 90 days: confirm procurement timeline and decision owner before closing the meeting.

Decision log (how to capture decisions in the doc):
- Row format (single line per decision): Date | Decision | Owner | Due date | Success metric | Status.
- Always assign an owner — meetings without owners are follow-up leaks.

Follow-up checklist (post-meeting):
- Within 2 business days: circulate meeting minutes + decision log (owner: CSM).
- Within 5 business days: AE confirms commercial timeline and procurement contacts (owner: AE).
- Within 10 business days: SE delivers a technical remediation plan or POC proposal if flagged (owner: SE).
- 30-day checkpoint: 30-min sync to review progress on top 3 actions (owner: CSM).

Templates & snippets (copy/paste):
- Invite subject: "QBR — {{ACCOUNT_NAME}} — Align on top priorities and renewal posture (45m)"
- Pre-read blurb (email body): "Please find a short 1-pager attached with usage highlights and our proposed agenda. If there’s anything you want added, drop a note in the doc or reply to this email. Looking forward to aligning on outcomes."

Quick escalation rubric (operational):
- Health <60 OR security/regulatory open items => escalate to CS Manager + SRE lead within 24 hours.
- Renewal risk: If renewal >20% downside (AE estimate) schedule a renewal review w/ sales leader within 3 business days.

Common gotchas & notes-to-self:
- Don’t turn the QBR into a product demo — demos belong in a follow-up session unless the customer asks for it explicitly.
- Micro-commitments beat long-term promises. Prefer 30/60/90-day owners and measurable check-ins.
- Track 'ask friction' — if a customer repeatedly defers giving a decision owner, flag as higher churn risk.

Appendix: sample 60-second health summary template (for the slide or first page of the doc):
- Usage: "Active seats up 18% q/q; daily API calls +12%"
- Reliability: "p99 latency 220ms, incident rate stable"
- Adoption: "3 new flows live this quarter; 2 teams paused on pilot"
- Commercial: "Budget cycle runs April 2026; procurement engaged"

Revision history:
- 2026-02-20: First draft — Maya Chen.
- 2026-03-10: Updated pre-brief checklist and escalation thresholds — Liam Patel.

Notes: keep this intentionally terse. Use the decision log to force accountability. If you want a slide-deck version, see linked Confluence template (linked_artifacts).
